F1: All four goroutines inherit caller cancellation, so request completion can cancel legacy writes.
F2: Legacy errors are discarded after metric recording, and unrecovered panics in the new goroutines can crash the process.
F3: Create and Update storage failures populate the legacy histogram, while legacy DeleteCollection populates the storage histogram.
F4: Delete returns immediately on storage NotFound, leaving any legacy-only object undeleted.
F5: Legacy receives the original objInfo and recomputes updates against its own state, allowing divergence from storage.
F6: Unconditional forwarding of dry-run requests to legacy predates this change; moving those calls into goroutines did not introduce it.
